Here we discuss our individual patients problems with an aim to solve the patient’s clinical problem with collective current best evident based input.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis E blog also reflects my patient cantered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.I have been given this case to solve in an attempt to understand the topic of “patient clinical data analysis” to develop my competency in reading and comprehending clinical data including history, clinical findings,investigations and come up with diagnosis and treatment plan.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECase: A 77 year old female presented to\u0026nbsp; Ophthalmology opd with complaints\u0026nbsp; of\u0026nbsp; diminishion of vision in right eye.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHistory of present illness:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient was apparently asymptomatic 1 year back when she had nocturia due to which she went to the hospital and was diagnosed with diabetes for which she was medication. She takes Glimeperide 1mg and Metformin 500mg twice\u0026nbsp; daily\u0026nbsp; ( morning and evening)ever since.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient has itchy skin lesion over left foot since one year. She also complains of itching over genitals since one year.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe developed diminished vision 6 months back which is insidious in onset, gradual in progression. and associated with itching. Not associated with redness.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPast history :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EKnown case of hypertension since 1 year and takes tab losartan daily .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENot a known case of TB, asthma, epilepsy\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPersonal history :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMixed diet\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAppetite is reduced\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENormal bowel and bladder movements\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESleep is adequate\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo Addictions\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDaily routine :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBefore\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe used to wake up at 5:00 am. She walks 1\/2 a kilometer to buy milk. Then at 8:00 am after having breakfast, she goes and sits at a shop beside the house and returns home at 2:00 pm for lunch and then goes to sleep. After waking up, she has dinner and sleeps at 10:00 pm.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENow\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe used to wake up at 5:00 am. exam OSCE "},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003ECase\u003C\/b\u003E : A 77 yr old female with uncontrolled diabetes mellitus\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOSCE questions:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;1)\u0026nbsp;\u003Cb\u003ESteroid induced diabetes mellitus\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESteroid-induced diabetes mellitus is defined as an abnormal increase in blood glucose associated with the use of glucocorticoids in a patient with or without a prior history of diabetes mellitus.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe criteria for diagnosing diabetes by the American Diabetes Association\u0026nbsp; is\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;8 h fasting blood glucose ≥ 7.0 mmol\/L (126 mg\/dL),\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2 h post 75 g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) ≥ 11.1 mmol\/L (200 mg\/dL),\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHbA1c\u0026nbsp;≥ 6.5% or in patients with symptoms of hyperglycemic, a random plasma glucose of ≥ 11.1 mmol\/L (200 mg\/dL)\u003Cb\u003E.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe effect of glucocorticoids on glucose metabolism is likely the result of impairment of multiple pathways including beta cell dysfunction (sensitivity to glucose and ability to release insulin) and insulin resistance in other tissue.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003ERISK FACTORS:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EProposed risk factors for steroid-induced diabetes beyond cumulative dose and longer duration of steroid course include:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eolder age, family history, high body mass index and impaired glucose tolerance .\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe association with family history of diabetes is not well defined.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;compared the demographics and clinical characteristics of patients with new onset SIDM with those with type 2 diabetes with and without steroid treatment. Those individuals who developed new onset SIDM had significantly less family history of diabetes when compared with individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus and glucocorticoid treatment.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPATHOGENESIS\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EMolecular basis of glucocorticoid action on glucose regulation\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe insulin-mediated pathways of glycogen synthesis and protein degradation and synthesis are directly influenced by glucocorticoids . Skeletal muscle is responsible for the majority of insulin-mediated glucose uptake. Insulin recruits GLUT4 glucose transporters to the cell surface enabling glucose uptake into cell. Glucocorticoids impair insulin-mediated glucose uptake by directly interfering with components of the insulin signalling cascade, such as glycogen synthase kinase-3, glycogen synthase and GLUT4 translocation.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAn increase in protein degradation and decrease in protein synthesis is due to glucocorticoid inhibition of post-insulin receptor .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2) What is the mechanism of action of insulin at cellular level?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EInsulin acts on a glycoprotein- tyrosine kinase receptors on the cell membrane and it binds to the alpha subunit which leads to phosphorylation of beta subunit.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis leads to transport of GLUT RECEPTORS on to the cell membrane which in-turn transports glucose into the target cell( adipocyte and muscle cell)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003ELearning points:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETidal percussion in diaphragm palsy.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EClincical differentiation between type 1 and type diabetes mellitus.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDifferences between osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETreatment options for portal hypertension.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr
